plugins.name: guard
plugins.description: When a turn ends, guard asks the session to run its router subagent over the response; the router names which audit agents would actually find something in it — unsupported claims, deferrals the repo could answer, explanation the reader cannot follow, unnatural Korean, comments in the source it edited, AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md that drifted from a map into a payload, saved reference docs that filled up with local reasoning — each with a reason; they run in parallel and nothing is corrected until all of them have reported, so every audit judges the same text — then the ones that found something read the corrections once more. It also keeps the session off the network: documentation lookups go to an agent that reports where the document is — already saved, in the repository, or in a knowledge base the project configures — and fetches and saves the primary source only when the network is the only place it lives. One switch per agent, all off until you turn one on; whether a session starts with turn and plan auditing armed is itself a saved setting: the plan gate armed unless the project says otherwise, the turn audit muted until you arm it. A separate `interviewer` agent is not part of that: you talk to it directly in its own transcript before any work starts, and it questions you one at a time — testing what you said rather than guessing the rest — until the request is clear, then researches it and, when you close the interview, leaves one brief on disk for the session to act on. A `handover` skill writes a self-contained session handover before you clear the conversation, and the session `/clear` opens next is offered it: guard carries the file's path across that boundary and the session asks whether to read it. Claude Code and Codex. Requires Python 3.11+.

plugins.name: peers
plugins.description: A peer is a Claude Code session running somewhere else on this machine — another repository, another checkout, another project. This plugin finds the peer already serving a folder and reuses the context it has built up, or starts one there and tells you which folder is getting an agent before it does; the peer runs under that project's own permission settings, never a mode the plugin imposed. Tasks go out with a reply address written into them, because a peer's answer reaches you only if the peer sends it, and you are told when one finishes instead of waiting on it. Two peers can also be introduced to each other to settle a cross-repository question directly, with one of them named as the reporter. Background peers it started can be stopped when the work is done; a session you started yourself in a terminal is left to you. Claude Code only — Codex has no cross-session messaging. Requires the `claude` CLI and `uv`.
